text:
maya: Quick check — PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference/pull/987 is ready from my side but it's gated on the design/RFC (https://internal.redwood.com/rfcs/345). Can someone from arch confirm coverage? cc @liam @alex

liam: I skimmed RFC-345 earlier; it does cover KV-cache routing and fallback behavior. I left a couple inline comments on the PR about timeout semantics and rollout metrics.

alex: Thanks for the ping. Two things I'm looking for before I can add the arch label: 1) canary rollout config matches RFC-345 section 4.2, and 2) telemetry events for the new code paths are emitted (so Optimize can pick them up).

maya: Got it. I pushed a tiny update that mirrors the canary limits in the RFC and added placeholder telemetry events. I didn't want to merge without a formal arch ack — we use the `arch/approved` label to lift the gate.

liam: I can give formal ack after you address my timeout comment. Quick note: ensure the fallback to the smaller model preserves the same response schema (we don't want downstream parsing errors).

devops-bot: automated-checks: e2e ✅, lint ✅, canary-config ❌ — missing telemetry.event entries. Full report: https://ci.redwood.com/987

alex: I just pushed the telemetry.event additions and a small schema compatibility test in tests/compat/test_fallback_schema.py. @liam can you re-review? If you're happy, please add `arch/approved` and I'll merge after CI goes green. :thumbsup:

maya: Timeline for product: if we can unblock today, we can start a dedicated capacity rollout tomorrow. If helpful, I can run a short sync at 3:00pm PT to walk through the changes.

liam: I'll do a final pass at 2:45pm PT. If the timeout fix + schema test look good, I'll add the `arch/approved` label.

alex: thanks — will watch CI and merge once the label is present and CI is green. :rocket:
